sections.thesis: Treasuries rallied last week as fears that higher borrowing costs could slow AI investment sent investors back to government bonds.

sentences.text: Treasuries rallied last week as fears that higher borrowing costs could slow AI investment sent investors back to government bonds.
The 10-year yield fell 0.146 percentage point to 5.097%, its biggest weekly decline since mid-February.
Traders still see a roughly 85% chance of a Fed hike by year-end, with the next meeting on October 27-28.

sections.thesis: The dollar index slipped after Fed Chair Warsh said he does not prejudge meetings.

sentences.text: The dollar index slipped after Fed Chair Warsh said he does not prejudge meetings.
Bets on an October hike fell to about 16% from near 28%, while a December hike is still priced near 90%.
Fed officials are silent from Saturday until the October 27-28 meeting.

sections.thesis: Big Tech had its biggest weekly drop since the April 2025 tariff announcement on AI jitters, with the Nasdaq 100 down 5.5% after a 2.5% fall on Friday.

sentences.text: Big Tech had its biggest weekly drop since the April 2025 tariff announcement on AI jitters, with the Nasdaq 100 down 5.5% after a 2.5% fall on Friday.
CoreWeave shed almost 12% on Friday and the S&P 500 closed 1.1% lower.
The PHLX semiconductor index slid 3.8% to its longest losing streak since 2008.

sections.thesis: Oil hit a five-month high after Saudi-led forces reported destroying missiles fired at the kingdom's energy hubs.

sentences.text: Oil hit a five-month high after Saudi-led forces reported destroying missiles fired at the kingdom's energy hubs.
Brent settled 3.7% higher at $109.86 after touching $110 for the first time since May, and WTI settled up 3.5% at $101.41.
Two tankers were struck northeast of Jubail, and diesel futures settled at $4.90 a gallon.
